timer.counter: Eight-bit wrapping down-counter; transition from 01 to 00 sets TCR7 and the following event changes 00 to FF.
timer.prescaler: Seven-bit divider by 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, or 128; reset and a TCR3 write-one pulse initialize it to 7F.

clock_modes.01: internal E cycles while TIMER is high

timer.wait_vector: An enabled timer request accepted from WAIT uses 1FF6:1FF7; normal timer and INT2 share 1FF8:1FF9.
timer.external_edge: Manufacturer Q&A QA635-315A resolves the event-input edge as rising.
timer.tdr_access: Manufacturer Q&A QA635-314A states that a write during countdown restarts from the written byte while a read leaves countdown undisturbed.

reference.locator: HD63705V0 section 2.3, figures 2-4 and 2-5, and tables 2-1 through 2-3, printed pages 110-112; Q&A QA635-314A, handbook printed page 902; Q&A QA635-315A, handbook printed page 903; Q&A QA635-316A, handbook printed page 904

gpio.ports: Ports A, B, and C have eight bits; Port D has seven bits. Every bit has a direction bit and reset selects input.
gpio.multiplexing: D3 is synchronous Tx, D4 is Rx, D5 is CK, and D6 shares the INT2 package pin. Selecting Tx/Rx/CK both overrides the active pin direction and writes the corresponding DDRD direction; QA635-302A says that stored direction remains after SCI is disabled. D0-D2 and D6 remain ordinary GPIO during SCI.
gpio.readback: The common-port diagram documents latch readback for outputs and pin readback for inputs.

reference.locator: HD63705V0 terminal description and section 2.8, printed pages 105-106 and 124-125; Q&A QA635-302A through QA635-304A, handbook printed pages 890-892; Q&A QA635-328A, handbook printed page 916

sci.format: Eight-bit synchronous transfer, least-significant bit first; transmit changes on negative CK edges and receive samples positive CK edges.
sci.clock: SCR5:SCR4 selects disabled GPIO, internal clock/output, or external clock/input. Sixteen documented clock widths are powers of two from 1 us through 32768 us at a 4-MHz oscillator.
sci.timer2: The internal 15-bit transfer-clock generator sets SSR6 on each negative edge even while the serial shifter uses external CK.
sci.completion: SSR7 sets on completion of either eight-bit transmit or receive; an SDR access with SCR5 one clears it, starts transmission for a write, and arms initial reception.

reference.locator: HD63705V0 section 2.4 and figures 2-6 through 2-8, printed pages 113-117

operating_modes.mcu: NUM low selects single-chip execution from the internal 1000-1FFF EPROM and 0040-00FF RAM.
operating_modes.wait: WAIT stops the CPU while timer and SCI continue; an enabled request vectors, with the timer-specific wait vector.
operating_modes.stop: STOP halts oscillator, CPU, and peripherals and only INT or enabled INT2 wakes the core. The normalized implementation follows figure 2-18 by setting TDR to F0, clearing timer/SCI request flags, and setting their masks. Section 2.9 prose and table 2-5 instead say registers are retained except TCR6/TCR7, so exact silicon STOP register state is UNDEFINED_BY_DOCUMENTATION.
operating_modes.standby: STBY low asynchronously resets internal registers and makes I/O high impedance while retaining RAM; normalized standby_n_i represents the digital boundary.
operating_modes.eprom: The digital programming interface maps twelve external EPROM addresses to 1000-1FFF and implements all five table-2-9 states: ordinary +5-V read, output disable, VPP programming, VPP verification with CE don't-care, and program/verify disable.

reference.locator: HD63705V0 sections 2.9 and 2.10 and tables 2-5 through 2-9, printed pages 125-136

memory_control.pc: The CPU masks every program-counter result to fourteen bits.
memory_control.stack: The physical stack wraps in 00C0-00FF and resets to 00FF; documented nesting leaves 00C0 as the wrap boundary.
memory_control.unmapped: The handbook defines no external MCU-mode memory bus. Q&A QA635-338A prohibits access to the IC-test area at 0013-001F but does not define a stable result; other unused ranges likewise have no specified read data. The FPGA wrapper returns FF and ignores writes in both classes without claiming an undocumented silicon read value.

reference.locator: HD63705V0 sections 2.1 and 2.2 and figures 2-1 through 2-3, printed pages 107-109; Q&A QA635-338A, handbook printed page 926

implementation_scope.rtl: rtl/hd6305/hd63705v0_mcu.sv implements the single-chip digital MCU boundary, a stated figure-2-18 STOP normalization, and normalized EPROM programming pins.
implementation_scope.model: model/hd63705v0_device.py independently classifies every physical address and models memory, GPIO, timer, interrupts, synchronous SCI/Timer2, normalized STOP state changes per E cycle, and the combinational EPROM table.
implementation_scope.verification: Model and RTL suites exhaust all 16384 physical addresses and all 192 retained RAM bytes; all 256 TCR writes, 2048 counter/divider pairs, all 32 source/divider combinations, request/mask/TDR access, reset and wait-vector behavior; all 248 GPIO bit truth-table combinations plus fixed Port-D readback, WAIT/STOP retention, and all 512 SCR/initial-DDR combinations; and cover external interrupt priority, eight-bit serial transfer, normalized STOP/STBY, and all five table-2-9 EPROM states.
implementation_scope.undefined_policy: IC-test-area and unused read values, SDR reset data, and the STOP register state disputed by section 2.9/table 2-5 versus figure 2-18 are deterministic FPGA normalizations, not silicon-equivalence claims.
analog_exclusions: EPROM charge programming, voltage margins, and retention
